subject: Privacy terms: signature path, subprocessor list, and incident-notify protocol
messages:
From: Tom Baylor <procurement@fintechco.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Privacy terms & signature — next steps

Connor —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our redlines to Redwood's standard DPA (see fintechco_dpa_redlines.pdf). Two quick asks so we can move to signature:

- Can you provide the current subprocessor registry (or a link) and confirm subprocessors for EU-data processing?
- We need explicit breach-notification timing in the DPA; our legal team expects an initial notice within 24 hours of detection and a follow-up with details within 72 hours. Is that something Redwood can commit to?
- DocuSign logistics: we prefer the DPA executed first with an Annex A listing subprocessors attached to the envelope. Can you confirm who will create and send the envelope and whether Redwood can CC procurement@fintechco.com?
- Finally, please send current SOC 2 Type II report or a download link for our review.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants this wrapped to meet our onboarding window.

Thanks,
Tom Baylor
Procurement Lead — FinTechCo
procurement@fintechco.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baylor <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privacy terms & signature — next steps

Marissa / Aditya — looping you in with Tom's redlines (attached). Key asks from FinTechCo: subprocessors list, breach notification timing (they asked 24h initial / 72h follow-up), and DocuSign flow with Annex A attached. Also asked for SOC2.

My thoughts / proposed approach:
- Provide current subprocessor CSV (I've attached redwood_subprocessors_20270607.csv) and a short note explaining our standard carve-out process for adding new subprocessors (30-day notice + opt-out).
- For breach notifications: offer a two-tier commitment — an initial customer notice within 24 hours of detection for material incidents affecting customer data, and a more detailed notice "no later than 72 hours" with available facts. That maps to FinTechCo's ask but gives us some operational wiggle room.
- Marissa: can you draft a short paragraph we can insert under "Incident Notification" that reads along the lines of: "We will use reasonable efforts to provide initial notice to the customer within 24 hours of detection and, where possible, a more comprehensive notification no later than 72 hours from detection, subject to ongoing investigation and legal constraints."
- DocuSign: I'd like Redwood to prepare the envelope (DPA + Annex A). Tom asked to be CC'd. Recommend we send the envelope, but mark the Annex A as 'dynamic' so we can attach the subprocessor CSV. Aditya — is this acceptable for your sales timeline?

I'll wait for Marissa's redline language. If OK, I can prepare the envelope and send today/tomorrow so procurement can get it signed by EOW.

Connor O'Brien
Sr. Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baylor <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privacy terms & signature — next steps

Connor / Aditya —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed FinTechCo's redlines. We can reasonably accept most edits but need to push back (or clarify) on a few items before sending to signature:

1) Breach notification timing: do NOT agree to an absolute "24 hours" for full detail. Instead propose this language: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide initial notice to Customer of a confirmed security incident affecting Customer data within 24 hours of detection, and will provide reasonably available details as they are identified, with a more detailed update no later than 72 hours from detection where practicable. Where legal constraints or investigative needs require, Redwood may provide a preliminary notice followed by additional updates." This preserves the customer's expectations while allowing incident-response steps.

2) Indemnity / liability: push back on any language that creates unlimited or uncapped obligations tied solely to processing. We'll offer standard liability caps aligned with the main agreement.

3) Subprocessors: fine to attach Annex A to the DocuSign envelope and include the CSV as a live Annex (we should timestamp it). Add a one-line commitment: "Customer will be notified of additions to Annex A in accordance with the Subprocessors section and may object within 30 days."

4) Evidence & cooperation: add specific cooperation commitments (e.g., forensics access, preservation of logs) but limit the scope to what is reasonably necessary and subject to legal restrictions.

Please use the following redline paragraph for the DPA incident-notify section (you can paste it into the document):

"Incident Notification (proposed): Redwood will notify Customer of confirmed incidents affecting Customer data and will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide an initial notification within 24 hours of detection. Redwood will provide further details as they become available and, where practicable, will provide a substantive update no later than 72 hours after detection. Redwood's obligations to disclose information shall be subject to applicable laws and reasonable measures to preserve the integrity of the investigation. Redwood will cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests for forensic information where such cooperation does not compromise ongoing legal obligations or third-party rights."

If you want, I can prepare the marked-up DPA response (redwood_dpa_response_marked.docx) and we can send a short cover note with the DocuSign envelope.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_dpa_response_marked.docx (Word, 18 KB)

Connor / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear proposed language — that version of the notification clause is acceptable to our legal team, subject to final wording in the executed DPA. Two housekeeping items before we route to signature:

- Please ensure Annex A (subprocessors) is attached to the DocuSign envelope as a static PDF (we need a permanent record), and include a one-line timestamp on the Annex.
- When you send the envelope, please CC procurement@fintechco.com and our security contact (security@fintechco.com). Also include a DocuSign reminder cadence (we generally appreciate a 3-day and a 7-day reminder).

If you can send the DocuSign envelope with the attached Annex A and the marked DPA by EOD Monday, our side will prioritize execution and aim to have signatures completed by end-of-day next Wednesday. Please send the envelope link once live.

Thanks —
Elena Ruiz
